extracted.intended_audience: general readers of Andrew Carnegie's autobiography; historians and readers interested in late-19th/early-20th memoirs
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative observations and practical advice embedded in Andrew Carnegie's autobiographical chapters describing encounters with literary, religious, and political figures (lecturing, criticism, municipal government, memorials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public speaking — need for elocution and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: He must fit himself for public speaking; 'He must get an elocutionist to give him lessons upon two or three points.' His first lecture 'was not a success, owing solely to his inability to speak well in public.' Later improvement after lessons caused his voice to fill the hall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take professional elocution lessons to correct specific defects; practise so the voice will project and reach large halls; remediate identifiable faults rather than rely on natural gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecture tone — avoid being 'too ministerial'
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Carnegie's blunt verdict on Arnold's first night: 'Too ministerial, Mr. Arnold, too ministerial.' Arnold remembered and felt it 'hit the nail on the head.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a sermonic or overly ministerial delivery in public lectures; tailor tone to audience expectations and purpose; solicit candid feedback and act on concise critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance humor and seriousness in lecturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule explained by Josh Billings, quoted by Arnold: 'You mustn't keep them laughing too long, or they will think you are laughing at them. After giving the audience amusement you must become earnest and play the serious rôle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure lectures so amusement opens or warms the audience, then transition into earnest material; avoid over-extending comic material which can undercut credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuously refresh material — invent new stories
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Yes, always. You can't lecture year after year unless you find new stories,' said the lecturer, describing the need to keep content fresh between tours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly develop new anecdotes and examples so repeated lectures remain engaging; maintain a running store of fresh items and retire overused bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of wording for comedic/persuasive effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A single 'indispensable word' can make a story 'crack like a whip'—the lecturer recounts waiting for an exact word that made a joke land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully choose the precise word or phrase for maximum effect; small lexical changes can determine whether an anecdote succeeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rhetorical devices and audience interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of using a rhetorical question sequence to engage the audience and set up a punchline: asking 'Who will tell me what these are?' to elicit responses and then deliver the comic turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ questions, pauses, and solicitations of audience response to involve listeners and build momentum toward key points or punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to criticism of transcendent works (e.g., Shakespeare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arnold believed he was 'incompetent to write upon, much less to criticize, Shakespeare. He believed it could not be successfully done. Shakespeare was above all, could be measured by no rules of criticism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise humility when approaching canonical or transcendent works; recognize limits of prescriptive rules and avoid forcing such works into rigid critical frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing/selecting sacred or classical texts — winnowing 'wheat from the chaff'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The Scriptures should be so dealt with. The gems from Confucius and others which delight the world have been selected with much care... We should have those portions selected and use the selections only.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate sacred or classical corpora by selecting exemplary passages and removing accretions that mislead or harm; favor annotated/selected editions over unfiltered compilations when instructing readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorial fundraising — selective private subscription
rubrics_metrics.description: On raising a memorial fund for Matthew Arnold: 'These friends quietly provided the necessary sum, as no public appeal could be thought of. No one could be permitted to contribute to such a fund except such as had a right to the privilege.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain memorials, prefer private, selective subscription from those deemed appropriate rather than public solicitation; preserve exclusivity and dignity of the memorial by restricting contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership qualities — tenacity, temper control, calm judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of political figures: lack of 'tenacity of purpose essential to command'; inability to control temper was 'fatal' to leadership; the indispensable leader is 'a man of calm, sober, unclouded judgment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate or cultivate leaders for steadiness, ability to control temperament, tenacity, and sober judgment rather than mere eloquence or brilliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal government best practices and civic pride
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for British municipal life: 'The best people are on the councils of British towns, elected by popular vote... That invaluable asset, city pride, is created... Councilorships are sought... All gave their time gratuitously.' Advocacy for paying legislators and daytime sittings for Parliament to broaden participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote local civic engagement by encouraging permanent residence and pride in place, accessible council service (even unpaid civic service can be valuable), and structural reforms (remuneration for legislators, daytime sittings) to widen participation and improve governance.
